claims.text: UTMB contracted in December 2024 for a platform giving it a secure way to work with generative AI models.
claims.quote: In December 2024, U.T. Medical Branch - Galveston (UTMB) entered into a Master Subscription Agreement (MSA) with Qualified Health for the Qualified Operating System (qOS) platform and Qualified GPT, which is a secure interface to interact with Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) models and applications.

claims.text: The first agreement was set at 825,000 dollars and needed no Board approval.
claims.quote: The initial Agreement had a contract value set at $825,000, which was within the institution's delegated authority threshold and did not require Board approval, and the term was one year with two 12-month renewal options thereafter.

claims.text: The first amendment raised the value to 4,250,000 dollars and still sat inside the same delegated authority.
claims.quote: In October 2025, UTMB entered into the First Amendment of the MSA, which transitioned to Qualified Health Enterprise AI Platform and increased the value to $4,250,000, remaining within the institution's delegated authority threshold.

claims.text: The third amendment extends the platform to all seven University of Texas System health related institutions, funded by an initiative the 89th Legislature appropriated.
claims.quote: This Third Amendment extends the Qualified Health Technology Platform to all seven U.T. System Health-Related Institutions (HRIs) and will be funded by U.T. System under the UT-REAL-Health AI initiative appropriated by the 89th Texas Legislature.

claims.text: The third amendment adds 5,600,000 dollars and brings the agreement to 9,850,000 dollars, running to October 30th, 2027.
claims.quote: The term of the Third Amendment is October 31, 2025 through October 30, 2027, and the additional value is $5,600,000 bringing the total value of the Agreement with Qualified Health to $9,850,000.

claims.text: The agenda book states the agreement was competitively procured.
The item is number 65 on the consent agenda and names the contracting institution.
claims.quote: 65. Contract (funds going out) - U.T. Medical Branch - Galveston: Amendment to Agreement with Qualified Health, PBC, to provide AI technology platform

claims.text: The initiative paying for the extension is carried in the system budget as a state general revenue funded program.
claims.quote: State General Revenue Funded programs include Lone Star Stroke, Texas Child Mental Health Care Consortium (TCMHCC), and REAL-Health-AI

claims.text: The meeting the item appears on opens with a public hearing opportunity.
claims.quote: Wednesday, August 12, 2026 1:00 p.m. Public Hearing Opportunity

claims.text: The document that carries all of this is the Board's own agenda book for its August meeting.
claims.quote: August 12-13, 2026 Meeting of the U.T. System Board of Regents - Consent Agenda

rejected.finding: That the UT Dell Medical Center approved at the same meeting is an AI-native hospital, reported by several outlets.
rejected.reason: The Regents' own agenda book never uses the words artificial intelligence in that item. It says digital technology, robotics, and automation, and a digitally enabled infrastructure. The AI-native framing is the coverage's and not the document's, so it is not available to this deck.

rejected.finding: That the Board approved consent agenda item 65 on August 12th.
rejected.reason: No minutes for the August 12th and 13th meeting are published. The agenda book shows the item was placed on the consent agenda and nothing on the public record shows what the Board did with it.

rejected.finding: Which seven health related institutions the extension reaches.
rejected.reason: The item says all seven and does not enumerate them. Naming them would be a claim the document does not make.
